saints.name: St. Lea of Rome
saints.title: Widow
saints.shortBlurb: A Roman widow who left the world for a life of prayer and penance, held up by St. Jerome as an example above worldly greatness…
biography: Lea was a noble Roman widow of the fourth century, known to us only through her friend St. Jerome. Left wealthy by an early widowhood, she renounced the world and joined the circle of ascetic women gathered about St. Marcella, shedding her riches and standing to live as a servant among consecrated virgins.

In time she became the superior of the community. Jerome recalls that she exchanged her rich attire for sackcloth, ceased to command others that she might obey, dwelt in a corner with a few pieces of furniture, and spent her nights in prayer, instructing her companions by example rather than by words.

She died in 384, while Jerome and Marcella were reading the seventy-third psalm together. In the letter that is our whole knowledge of her, Jerome set her hidden and holy death against the pomp of a Roman consul lately buried amid pagan honors, praising her as one who chose Christ over the world.
saints.knownFor: Her hidden life of penance, commended by St. Jerome.
